opal.name: Opal
jet.name: Jet
opal.dialogue.Introduction: You're the farmer! Of course you are, you've got the hands. Come in, mind the glass, everything sharp is Jet's.$h#$b#Opal Corrie. The quiet one's my brother, Jet. Our mother named us after her glass. Don't. We've heard it.$u
opal.dialogue.Mon: Monday! I've drawn three windows before breakfast and Jet's thrown out two of them. That's a good morning, for us.$h
opal.dialogue.Tue: Twenty years of meetings about glass. Not one of them was made of glass.$u
opal.dialogue.Wed: I do the talking, Jet does the cutting. Between us we're one perfectly reasonable person.$h
opal.dialogue.Thu: Afternoons I walk the plaza and look up at the windows. Half of them want replacing. The other half want me.$u
opal.dialogue.Fri: Bea remembers us! Well, she remembers being nine and us shouting at each other across the plaza. Same thing really.$h
opal.dialogue.Sat: Saturday! I take the bus to Pelican Town. Pierre's, the Saloon, a bit of gossip. Jet stays here and calls it peace.$h
opal.dialogue.Sun: Mabel never worked on a Sunday. So of course we always did. Habit's a funny old thing.$0
opal.dialogue.Mon2: Lupini had one coat and no money and he painted the lake purple. We thought he was mad. We were right, and look at him now.$u
opal.dialogue.Wed2: Tobin says his kiln runs hotter than ours. His kiln is a pile of bricks with opinions.$u
opal.dialogue.Fri2: Robin did the studio beautifully. Have I told her? I've told her. I'll tell her again on Saturday.$h
opal.dialogue.Mon4: Our mother worked at that bench for twenty-four summers. I learned to talk sitting under it, Jet learned to cut. You can guess which of us was listening.$l
opal.dialogue.Tue4: Corrie Glass did station roofs, hotel lobbies, a cathedral in the south. I ran the money, Jet ran the workshop. By the end neither of us touched the glass.$s
opal.dialogue.Thu4: Emmett has a song about the Vale with a verse about a woman who "held the morning to the light". That's Mabel. He doesn't know. I've never told him. I like hearing it.$l
opal.dialogue.Sat4: Margot thinks Corrie Glass replaced too much and mended too little. She's right, which is very annoying. I enjoy arguing with her enormously.$u
opal.dialogue.Tue6: I went up to the graveyard yesterday. Bram carved her stone, you know. He put a little sun on it. She'd have said it was too sweet. I love it.$s
opal.dialogue.Thu6: When the company sold I signed the papers with a pen that cost more than my first kiln. Then I came home and cried in Bea's tea room. Don't tell Jet.$s
opal.dialogue.Mon8: Twenty years of signing things. When we came home my hands didn't know what to do with a cutter. They're remembering. Mostly.$l
opal.dialogue.Wed8: Jet hasn't said one unkind word to me in sixty years. He just looks. The looks are worse.$u
opal.dialogue.Fri8: You're good for us, you know. We argue less when you're about. We argue better.$h
opal.dialogue.spring_Mon: Spring light's thin but honest. You can see every bubble in the glass.$0
opal.dialogue.summer_Mon: Summer! The long light. Mabel's season. Everything in here glows till nine o'clock.$h
opal.dialogue.fall_Tue: The Vale goes gold in fall and every window in it looks like it's on fire. I'd do the whole valley in amber if they'd let me.$h
opal.dialogue.winter_Mon: Winter. The kiln keeps us warm and Jet keeps it at exactly the right temperature. I keep the kettle.$0
opal.dialogue.winter_Fri: Off to Tobin's to argue about whose workshop's warmer. I'll lose. I always take biscuits.$u
opal.dialogue.spring_1: Spring! New light, new glass. Open a window, darling, it's a crime to keep the sun out.$h
opal.dialogue.summer_1: Summer. It's our birthday tomorrow. I'm telling you so you can't say you weren't told.$u
opal.dialogue.fall_1: Fall. Amber season. Jet's already sighing at me.$h
opal.dialogue.winter_1: Winter. Grey light, long nights, and more designs than I'll ever make. Lovely.$0
opal.dialogue.summer_2: Our birthday! Jet's pretending it isn't. He'll have made me something. He always does, and it's always better than mine.$h
opal.dialogue.rainy: Rain. All the colour's gone off the floor. I hate it. Jet loves it, he says he can see the glass properly. He's very strange.$u
opal.dialogue.AcceptGift_338: Refined quartz! You know what glass is? Sand that's been through something. Thank you, darling.$h
opal.dialogue.AcceptGift_595: A fairy rose! Look at that pink. I could never get that pink in glass. Never. Thank you!$h
opal.dialogue.AcceptGift_74: Oh. Oh, look at it. Every colour at once. I've been trying to do that for forty years.$l
opal.dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Positiv: For our birthday! You remembered. Jet, they remembered! He's pretending not to hear. Thank you, darling.$h
opal.dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Negativ: For our birthday! How kind. I'll find it a nice spot. Somewhere.$u
opal.gift.love: Oh, you darling! It's perfect. I'm going to put it where everyone can see it and tell them it was my idea.$h
opal.gift.like: Lovely! Thank you, really. Jet, look! He's not looking. Thank you!$h
opal.gift.dislike: Oh! Well. It's the thought. It is a thought, isn't it?$u
opal.gift.hate: Darling, no. Take that out of my studio before it touches anything.$a
jet.dialogue.Introduction: Hm. Don't touch the blue.$0#$b#Jet. Opal's brother. She'll have told you the rest.$0
jet.dialogue.Mon: Score, snap, grind. Same as Saturday.$0
jet.dialogue.Tue: She designs it. I make it possible. She'd tell you it's the other way round.$u
jet.dialogue.Wed: Glass doesn't forgive. Neither do I, much. We get on.$0
jet.dialogue.Thu: The lead's come in from the city. Opal ordered too much. She always orders too much.$0
jet.dialogue.Sat: Opal's gone to town. The studio's very big on Saturdays.$u
jet.dialogue.Sun: Our mother kept her bench clean. I keep it clean.$0
jet.dialogue.Mon2: I walk up to Fern's in the mornings. For the air.$0
jet.dialogue.Wed2: Tobin's kiln runs nine degrees cooler than he thinks. I won't tell him.$u
jet.dialogue.Fri2: Lupini gave Opal a painting once. The purple lake. She laughed at it. I kept it.$l
jet.dialogue.Mon4: Learned to cut at that bench. Under it, first. Picking up offcuts.$l
jet.dialogue.Tue4: In the city I had forty people cutting glass. I didn't cut any.$s
jet.dialogue.Thu4: Margot's right about the company. Don't tell Opal I said so.$u
jet.dialogue.Sat4: You've a steady hand. Score it like you mean it.$h
jet.dialogue.Tue6: Mabel's up the hill. I go on Tuesdays. Opal goes when she's upset. We don't go together.$s
jet.dialogue.Thu6: Bram Fairlie lived next door. He carved while we cut. He didn't talk either.$l
jet.dialogue.Mon8: Opal talks so I don't have to. Good arrangement. Sixty years.$u
jet.dialogue.Wed8: Here. An offcut. Blue. You can touch this one.$h
jet.dialogue.Fri8: You come in, you sit, you don't fill the quiet. Best customer we've had.$h
jet.dialogue.spring_Wed: Spring light's thin. Good for checking cuts.$0
jet.dialogue.summer_Thu: Summer. The kiln's hot, the studio's hot. Opal's hotter.$u
jet.dialogue.winter_Tue: Winter. The kiln stays lit. Opal goes to Tobin's. Quiet.$l
jet.dialogue.spring_1: Spring. Windows open. Dust in the light.$0
jet.dialogue.summer_1: Summer. Tomorrow's the birthday. Don't mention it.$u
jet.dialogue.fall_1: Fall. Leaves in the gutters again.$0
jet.dialogue.summer_2: Another year. Opal will make a fuss. Let her.$l
jet.dialogue.rainy: Rain. No colour on the floor. You can see the glass properly.$0
jet.dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Positive: For the birthday. ...Thank you. Don't tell Opal I liked it. She'll gloat.$l
corrie-event.opal2h.01: A packing crate in the middle of Opal's half, straw everywhere. Opal is on her knees in it, lifting out lamps: chrome, brass, a glass globe the size of a melon. Jet is at his bench, not looking.
corrie-event.opal2h.02: The last of the flat in Zuzu City. Jet said leave them. I said, Jet, they're Italian.$u
corrie-event.opal2h.03: She stands up with the biggest one: a chandelier dripping crystal.
corrie-event.opal2h.04: You! You have a house. Take one. Take this one.$h
corrie-event.opal2h.05: Where would I even put it?
corrie-event.opal2h.06: It's a bit much for a farmhouse.
corrie-event.opal2h.08: She looks at the chandelier, at you, at the chandelier, and laughs until she has to sit down on the crate.
corrie-event.opal2h.09: Over the cows! They'd look wonderful.$u
corrie-event.opal2h.10: It is, isn't it. Everything we owned was a bit much. That was rather the point.$s
corrie-event.opal2h.13: It won't go through a farmhouse door.$0
corrie-event.opal2h.14: ...It didn't go through ours either. They brought it in through the window.$u
corrie-event.opal2h.15: She puts the chandelier back in the straw and digs out the smallest thing in the crate.
corrie-event.opal2h.16: Here. The little one. It's the only one that was ever any use.$l
corrie-event.opal4h.01: Opal is behind the counter with a letter in one hand and a glossy catalogue in the other. Jet is cutting. She reads aloud, in a voice:
corrie-event.opal4h.02: 'Corrie Classic. The authentic stained-glass look. Self-adhesive.' Self-adhesive!$a
corrie-event.opal4h.03: The firm that bought us. They've put our name on a sticker. Mabel's name. On a sticker you put on a bathroom window.$a
corrie-event.opal4h.05: Does it matter what they call it?
corrie-event.opal4h.07: With what? We sold them the name. Signed it away with a pen that cost more than my first kiln.$u
corrie-event.opal4h.09: ...No. You're right. It doesn't. That's the awful part.$s
corrie-event.opal4h.10: That's what Jet said. In fewer words.$l
corrie-event.opal4h.12: She stops. She looks at the catalogue for a long moment.
corrie-event.opal4h.13: It's not ours any more. That was the point.$s
corrie-event.opal4h.14: She drops it in the bin.
corrie-event.opal8h.01: The kiln is open, still ticking as it cools. Opal is standing in front of it holding a small panel in both hands: a sunflower, every piece cut and leaded by her, and a crack straight across the middle.
corrie-event.opal8h.02: My first one. All mine, start to finish. The first in twenty years. And it cracked in the kiln.$s
corrie-event.opal8h.03: Do you know what I'm frightened of? That my hands have forgotten. That we didn't come home to make things. We came home because they sold us, and we had nowhere else to go, and I'm just very good at talking about it.$s
corrie-event.opal8h.04: One crack doesn't mean your hands forgot.
corrie-event.opal8h.05: Show me how you made it.
corrie-event.opal8h.06: You came home because you wanted to.
corrie-event.opal8h.07: No. It means I rushed the cooling. I know that. I knew it this morning.$l
corrie-event.opal8h.08: She does: the cartoon, the cutting, the lead. Halfway through she stops.
corrie-event.opal8h.10: Did I? I'd like to believe that.$s
corrie-event.opal8h.11: In the doorway behind her is Jet, back from somewhere, holding his coat. He heard. He doesn't say anything.
corrie-event.opal8h.12: He takes the cracked panel from her gently and holds it up to the lamp. The crack throws a thin bright line across the floor.
corrie-event.opal8h.13: Mabel's first one cracked too. She kept it.$l
corrie-event.opal8h.15: She did! It's in the loft somewhere. Oh, Jet.$u
corrie-event.jet4h.01: Jet is at Mabel's bench with a cloth, wiping it down, though it's clean. Her pliers are laid out as they always are.
corrie-event.jet4h.03: I learned under it. Picking up offcuts. Then on her knee. Then beside her.$0
corrie-event.jet4h.04: She'd put my hand on the cutter and press. 'Like you mean to break it, and you won't.'$l
corrie-event.jet4h.06: She sounds like a good teacher.
corrie-event.jet4h.08: He puts a hand on the stool, then takes it away.
corrie-event.jet4h.10: She was. Opal got the talking. I got the hands.$l
corrie-event.jet4h.11: You're the only one who doesn't ask.$h
corrie-event.jet4h.12: He folds the cloth, squares her pliers by a fraction, and goes back to the light table.
corrie-event.jet6h.01: Jet is coming down the ladder from the loft with a box on his shoulder, coughing in the dust. More boxes are stacked at its foot.
corrie-event.jet6h.04: He hands you a box. It's full of things the twins left behind twenty years ago: a cracked mug, their school reports, a pair of tiny safety glasses.
corrie-event.jet6h.05: At the bottom: a book with a cloth cover, its corners worn round. Jet goes still.
corrie-event.jet6h.07: He turns the pages: windows, years of them, each drawn and coloured and signed M.C. The last page is a window of the Vale at dawn, the sun coming up over gold trees, the river running down the middle. It's half coloured in. The other half is pencil.
corrie-event.jet6h.08: She never finished it. She was ill by then. We left it in the loft when we boarded up.$s
corrie-event.jet6h.12: He looks at you a long time.
corrie-event.jet6h.14: She'll cry. Then she'll want to change it.$u
corrie-event.jet6h.15: He closes the book very carefully.
corrie-event.jet6h.16: He puts the book on Mabel's bench, square to its edge, and goes back up the ladder.
corrie-event.jet8h.01: Raised voices before the door's even shut. Opal on her side of the line, Jet on his, for real this time: a crate of her sketches has slid over the line into his offcuts.
corrie-event.jet8h.02: It's three inches, Jet! Three inches of floor!$a
corrie-event.jet8h.04: It's Mabel's floor! You drew that line in the first week of the company and you've been standing behind it ever since!$a
corrie-event.jet8h.05: Work at Mabel's bench. Both of you.
corrie-event.jet8h.06: Rub out a bit of the line.
corrie-event.jet8h.07: Why did you draw the line?
corrie-event.jet8h.11: With what? It's paint. Jet painted it. Of course he did.$u
corrie-event.jet8h.12: So I'd have somewhere that was mine.$s
corrie-event.jet8h.13: Jet gets a scraper from his bench and, without a word, scrapes a gap in the line by Mabel's bench.
corrie-event.jet8h.15: ...I know. I've always known. I went anyway, and you came, and I never once asked you.$s
corrie-event.jet8h.17: Opal steps through the gap into the middle. After a moment, so does he.
corrie-event.jet10h.01: Jet is sitting at Mabel's bench. You've never seen anyone sit there. Her pattern book is open at the last page; beside it, the window, finished: the Vale at dawn, the sun over the gold trees, the river.
corrie-event.jet10h.02: Finished it last night. Her lines. My cuts.$l
corrie-event.jet10h.03: Opal comes out in her dressing gown, sees him at the bench, and stops. She doesn't say anything at all, which is how you know.
corrie-event.jet10h.04: Jet stands, lifts the panel, and the three of you carry it to the big window. He fits it into the frame himself.
corrie-event.jet10h.05: The sun comes through it. The Vale at dawn lands on the floor across the middle of the studio, right where the line used to be.
corrie-event.jet10h.07: Thank you for holding the ladder.$h
corrie-event.jet10h.08: She'd be proud of you both.
corrie-event.jet10h.09: Now you can make your own.
corrie-event.jet10h.11: She'd say we took our time.$s
corrie-event.jet10h.14: He shows you a drawing: a window for your farmhouse.
corrie-event.jet10h.15: Nobody says anything for a long time.
corrie-event.opal6h.01: Opal is standing in front of the Exhibition Hall with a sketchbook held up against the light, squinting from it to the dusty windows and back.
corrie-event.opal6h.02: There you are! Stand here. No, here. Now look up.$h
corrie-event.opal6h.03: Those windows went in the year we were born. Plain glass, cheap, because the Vale couldn't afford anything else. Mabel said she'd do them properly one day. She never got round to it.$0
corrie-event.opal6h.04: She turns the sketchbook round: the Hall's windows redrawn, each one a season of the Vale, in coloured pencil.
corrie-event.opal6h.05: Spring, summer, fall, winter. Four windows. I've been drawing them for forty years. On napkins, in meetings. On a contract once.$l
corrie-event.opal6h.07: Who would you have to ask?
corrie-event.opal6h.09: They are, aren't they! I'm not even going to pretend to be modest.$h
corrie-event.opal6h.10: Lupini, I suppose. He'd say yes and then forget. And somebody would have to open the place first.$u
corrie-event.opal6h.11: ...For a building nobody goes in. Yes. Why not.$l
corrie-event.opal6h.13: Twenty years ago I'd have had a team of forty on this by Friday. Now it's me, and Jet, and our hands. If they still work.$s
corrie-event.jet2h.01: Mist on the gardens. Jet is at the side of Fern's seedhouse with one pane out of its frame, a putty knife in his hand. He doesn't turn round.
corrie-event.jet2h.03: He fits a new pane, runs his thumb along the putty, and steps back to look. A long quiet.
corrie-event.jet2h.04: Does Fern know you do this?
corrie-event.jet2h.07: She thinks the wind's very careful.$u
corrie-event.jet2h.09: You hold the pane while he putties it in.
corrie-event.jet2h.11: Old glass. Somebody cared about this house once.$l
corrie-event.jet2h.12: He takes an offcut of blue glass from his apron and holds it out to you.
corrie-event.jet2h.14: The seedhouse door opens behind you and Fern looks out, yawning, at a pane that's whole. By then he's gone.
corrie-event.opal6hhall.01: Opal has her sketchbook open on the reception desk: the Hall's windows redrawn, each one a season of the Vale, in coloured pencil. Lupini is pretending not to be impressed.
corrie-event.opal6hhall.02: Spring, summer, fall, winter. Four windows. I've been drawing them for forty years. On napkins, in meetings. On a contract once.$l
corrie-event.opal6hhall.03: And what would four windows cost a poor gallery?$u
corrie-event.opal6hhall.04: For you? Far too much. And you'd be getting a bargain, and you'd know it, and you'd...$h
corrie-event.opal6hhall.08: He had one coat and no money when we met him. Now look at him, running a gallery.$u
corrie-event.opal6hhall.09: She hasn't changed. Not one bit. Thank goodness.$h
corrie-event.opal10hhall.01: The gallery is empty and dim. Opal and Jet are standing in the middle of the floor, not talking, which you've never seen.
corrie-event.opal10hhall.02: The sun comes up. Through the first of the new windows, above the door behind you, colour comes across the floor: a pool of spring green and gold that slides slowly over the tiles as the sun climbs.
corrie-event.opal10hhall.03: Spring. The first of the four.$l
corrie-event.opal10hhall.06: She takes your arm on one side and Jet's on the other.
corrie-event.opal10hhall.07: All three of ours. You held the ladder.$h
corrie-event.opal10hhall.08: It's the most beautiful thing in the Vale.
corrie-event.opal10hhall.12: ...She'd say the lead's too thick. And then she'd cry.$l
corrie-event.opal10hhall.13: Nobody says anything until it's reached the far wall.
corrie-event.opal10h.01: The tea room is empty and dim. Opal and Jet are standing by the tea tables, not talking, which you've never seen. In the wall above them is a new window.
corrie-event.opal10h.02: The sun comes up. Colour comes through the new window and across the tea tables: spring green and gold, sliding slowly as the sun climbs.
corrie-event.opal10h.03: Spring. The first of the four.$l
corrie-event.opal10h.06: She takes your arm on one side and Jet's on the other.
corrie-event.opal10h.07: All three of ours. You held the ladder.$h
corrie-event.opal10h.08: Bea brings three cups of tea and a fourth for herself, and sits down, which she never does.
corrie-event.opal10h.09: My aunt always wanted a window like that.$0
corrie-event.opal10h.10: I know. She told me. I was nine.$l
corrie-letter.opalletterhall: Come to the Hall at six. Don't be late, the sun won't wait.^^   -Opal

corrie-letter.opalletterhouse: Come to Bea's at six. Don't be late, the sun won't wait.^^   -Opal

corrie-event.bench_book: Mabel's bench, worn pale where her arms rested. Her pattern book lies on it now, closed, square to the edge.
bea.name: Bea
bea.gift.love: Oh, now that's for me, is it? Really for me? ...Thank you. This one's staying out of the kitchen.$h
bea.gift.like: That'll go straight in the kitchen. Thank you, really.$h
bea.gift.dislike: Ah. More work. Just what I needed.$u
bea.gift.hate: Did you find that in my drains? Take it back to them.$a
bea.gift.neutral: Thanks. I'll find it a shelf. The inn's mostly shelves.$0
bea.dialogue.Introduction: A guest! Or a lost hiker. Either way, there's tea.$h#$b#I'm Bea. This is the Vale House: inn, tea room, and post office when the post remembers us. If you need anything, I'm the one shouting from the kitchen.$u
bea.dialogue.Mon: Monday. The day everyone who stayed the weekend remembers they have jobs. Lovely people. Terrible tippers.$u
bea.dialogue.Tue: It has eleven rooms, two of them with roofs. I'm working on a third. The roof, not the room.$u
bea.dialogue.Wed: Wednesday's when I count the spoons. We had forty. We have thirty-one. I suspect Emmett, or the river.$0
bea.dialogue.Thu: Thursday's Pierre's day. You'd think a valley that grows everything would grow flour. It doesn't. I've asked.$u
bea.dialogue.Fri: Friday night, Emmett plays by the fire and everyone sings the wrong words. Come along. You'll fit right in.$h
bea.dialogue.Sat: Saturdays I get the day-trippers. They sit in the tea garden and tell me how peaceful it is here. They've never seen the plumbing.$u
bea.dialogue.Sun: The tea room shuts at noon on Sundays. Then I walk down to the lake and stand there until I forget the laundry. Takes about an hour.$0
bea.dialogue.Mon2: Lupini? He's run a tab since before I was born. I'm told it's an honour.$u
bea.dialogue.Wed2: The cups are Tobin's, every one. They weigh about as much as a brick, and I won't use any others. Don't tell him.$u
bea.dialogue.Fri2: Fern brings flowers for the tables every morning and they're dead by supper. 'They're wildflowers, Bea.' Yes, Fern. I'd noticed.$a
bea.dialogue.Mon4: My great-aunt ran this place for fifty years. I came to sell it. That was eight years ago. I keep meaning to put the sign up.$s
bea.dialogue.Tue4: I used to manage a hotel in Zuzu City. Four hundred rooms, and I didn't know a single guest's name. Here I know everyone's, and what they take in their tea.$0
bea.dialogue.Wed4: Emmett and I have been friends five years and arguing for all of them. He says my pies are too sweet. He's eaten forty.$u
bea.dialogue.Thu4: There's an attic upstairs I haven't opened since I got here. My aunt's things. One of these days.$s
bea.dialogue.Fri4: You know you can stay the night? Proper bed, proper breakfast. The roof over that room's one of the good two.$h
bea.dialogue.Sat4: I know everything about everyone in the Vale. Who's sweet on whom, who owes what. I don't tell. That's the job.$u
bea.dialogue.Sun4: Nobody comes down to the lake on a Sunday but me and the herons. We've got an understanding.$0
bea.dialogue.Tue6: Do you know what I wanted to be, before hotels? Nothing. I never got round to wanting anything. Funny, that.$s
bea.dialogue.Thu6: The inn costs more than it makes. Don't look like that, it's always cost more than it makes. My aunt ran it on charm and soup.$u
bea.dialogue.Sat6: You're one of the few people who asks how I am and waits for the answer. I'm not used to it. Ask again sometime.$l
bea.dialogue.Mon8: Do you know what nobody asks an innkeeper? What she'd like for dinner.$s#$b#Soup, since you're wondering. It's always soup.$h
bea.dialogue.Tue8: I've started thinking of it as my inn. Not hers. It felt rude at first, like borrowing her coat.$l
bea.dialogue.Wed8: Fifty years of guests, and I'm the one who stayed. She'd have laughed at that.$h
bea.dialogue.Thu8: I bought something at Pierre's today for nobody but me. Peach jam. I'm going to eat it out of the jar.$h
bea.dialogue.Fri8: Stay for the fire tonight. Emmett's got a new song, and he's nervous, which means it's a good one.$h
bea.dialogue.Sat8: If I ever do sell this place, I'm telling the buyer about you. 'Comes with a farmer. Excellent at dishes.'$u
bea.dialogue.Sun8: You're always welcome here. I mean it the way my aunt meant it: there's a key under the third flowerpot, and I'll know if you use it.$h
bea.dialogue.spring_Tue: Spring cleaning. So far I've found three umbrellas, a set of false teeth and a sketchbook from fifty years ago. The teeth were in the sketchbook.$u
bea.dialogue.spring_Sat: The tea garden's open again. Spring, and the first wasp. He comes every year. I've named him Gerald.$u
bea.dialogue.summer_Wed: It's too hot for tea. People order it anyway. I've started putting ice in it and calling it a city thing.$u
bea.dialogue.summer_Sun: The lake's warm enough for paddling. I don't, obviously. But I think about it.$0
bea.dialogue.fall_Thu: The old tree's gone gold. Every visitor takes the same picture of it, and Lupini sighs at them. It's the best part of my week.$h
bea.dialogue.fall_Sat: Open House soon. I'll be doing tea for half the valley. Ask me how I feel about it in a week.$u
bea.dialogue.winter_Mon: Winter's quiet. No coach parties, no day-trippers, no Gerald. I miss Gerald.$s
bea.dialogue.winter_Fri: The fire's going all day now. Emmett's moved into the armchair. I may have to charge him rent.$u
bea.dialogue.spring_1: First of spring! I open every window in the place on the first, even the ones that stick. Especially those.$h
bea.dialogue.summer_1: Summer. The tea garden's open till dark now. Mind the wasps.$0
bea.dialogue.fall_1: Fall already. I start making soup today and don't stop till spring.$h
bea.dialogue.winter_1: Winter. The pipes will freeze, I'll hit them with a spoon, and they'll unfreeze. It's a ritual.$u
bea.dialogue.spring_22: Did someone tell you? It's my birthday. I've made my own cake. Again.$u
bea.dialogue.rainy: Rain. Good. Nobody wants to sit in the tea garden, so I get to sit in it. Under the awning, with the good biscuits.$h
bea.dialogue.AcceptGift_614: Proper tea! Not the dust I buy at Pierre's. I'm drinking this one myself, sitting down.$h
bea.dialogue.AcceptGift_221: Somebody else made a cake. For me. Sit down, we're having it now, and you're not paying.$l
bea.dialogue.AcceptGift_341: A tea set! Oh, it's beautiful. Don't tell Tobin. It's going in my room, where he'll never see it.$l
bea.dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Positive: For my birthday? You remembered. Nobody remembers. I usually have to drop hints the size of a coach.$h
bea.dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Negative: For my birthday. Well. It's the thought, and the thought was... a thought.$u
tobin.name: Tobin
tobin.gift.love: Now that's useful. Thank you. I mean it.$h
tobin.gift.hate: No. Take that away from my clay.$a
tobin.dialogue.Introduction: Mind the shelf. Everything on it's for sale, and nothing's insured.$0#$b#Tobin. I make the pots. Yes, Clay. It's a family trade. The name came first.$u
tobin.dialogue.Mon: Monday. Wet clay, cold hands. Good start.$0
tobin.dialogue.Tue: Firing day. Stand back from the kiln. Further. There.$0
tobin.dialogue.Wed: Somebody asked me what this bowl means. It means soup.$u
tobin.dialogue.Thu: Every cup at the Vale House is one of mine. Bea says they're too heavy. She drops them less.$u
tobin.dialogue.Fri: Kiln's lit. Workshop's too hot to stand in. I stand in it anyway. Someone has to.$0
tobin.dialogue.Sat: A painting hangs on a wall. A bowl gets used every day. Which one gets looked at more?$0
tobin.dialogue.Sun: Sundays I dig. The pit by the river. Good clay comes up red and stubborn. Like me.$u
tobin.dialogue.Mon2: We've argued about whether a bowl is art for fifteen years, Lupini and me. I'm winning. He doesn't know yet.$u
tobin.dialogue.Wed2: I made Emmett an ocarina. I regret it every day.$a
tobin.dialogue.Fri2: Fern brought me cornflowers to press into a glaze. I said no. They're on that jug. Don't tell her.$0
tobin.dialogue.Mon4: My family made plates and jugs for farmhouses. Four generations. Somewhere out there your grandmother ate off one.$h
tobin.dialogue.Tue4: Came here at thirty because of that kiln. Best one I'd seen. Fifteen years on, still the best. I've seen more since.$0
tobin.dialogue.Wed4: You hold a cup differently when somebody made it. You notice that? Most people don't.$0
tobin.dialogue.Thu4: Visitors walk past my shelf to get to Lupini's paintings. Fine. They stop on the way back. To buy a mug.$u
tobin.dialogue.Fri4: Hardwood burns hotter. Long, steady heat. That's the secret to a good glaze. That and swearing.$u
tobin.dialogue.Sat4: You've got clay hands. Don't argue. I can tell from here.$h
tobin.dialogue.Sun4: 'Land of Clay.' Lupini painted it at my pit. I pretend I don't like it. I go and look at it once a month.$l
tobin.dialogue.Tue6: People think useful means less. Less thought, less care. I put more care in a cup than he puts in a sky. Don't quote me.$a
tobin.dialogue.Thu6: Clint and I talk kilns. Two hours, maybe four words. Best conversation I've had all year.$h
tobin.dialogue.Sat6: I don't want my name on a wall. I'd just like somebody to look at a jug and see the hands that made it.$s
tobin.dialogue.Mon8: You're good company. You don't fill up the quiet. Not many people can stand a quiet.$h
tobin.dialogue.Tue8: Firing day. Stay a while, if you can stand the heat. I'll show you how to read the cones.$h
tobin.dialogue.Wed8: My father said a pot's finished when you forget you made it and just use it. I've never forgotten one.$s
tobin.dialogue.Thu8: Bea says I should price the good bowls to match the work. I'd never sell any. I'd be fine with that.$u
tobin.dialogue.Fri8: Somebody should make you a proper cup. Something with a bit of weight to it. I'll think about who.$u
tobin.dialogue.Sat8: Fifteen years I've argued with Lupini. I think I like the argument more than the winning.$h
tobin.dialogue.Sun8: Come down to the pit some Sunday. Bring a spade. Clay's honest. It shows you every mistake.$h
tobin.dialogue.spring_Wed: Spring. Clay's soft and the river's high. Too high. The pit floods every year and I dig it out every year.$0
tobin.dialogue.spring_Sat: Robin bought six planters. Six. I didn't know Pelican Town had that many windowsills.$u
tobin.dialogue.summer_Mon: Summer, the pots dry before I've finished them. You work fast or you work twice.$0
tobin.dialogue.summer_Thu: Hot day, hot kiln. I had my lunch in the river. Standing in it.$u
tobin.dialogue.fall_Tue: Open House is coming. I'll put out a table of bowls. People will walk past it to look at paintings. Every year.$s
tobin.dialogue.fall_Fri: Fall's the best time for firing. Cool air, dry wood. The kiln sings.$h
tobin.dialogue.winter_Wed: Winter. The kiln keeps this the warmest house in the Vale. Funny how many people drop in to look at bowls.$u
tobin.dialogue.winter_Sat: Clay's half frozen in the sacks. I warm it by the kiln like bread dough.$0
tobin.dialogue.spring_1: Spring. Digging season. My back's already complaining.$0
tobin.dialogue.summer_1: Summer. I'll be firing twice a week till fall. Bring water if you visit.$0
tobin.dialogue.fall_1: Fall. The best clay of the year comes up now. Don't ask me why. Clay doesn't explain itself.$u
tobin.dialogue.winter_1: Winter. The wheel's slow in the cold. So am I.$0
tobin.dialogue.winter_5: Birthday. The kiln's lit and the workshop's warm. That's all I ask.$h
tobin.dialogue.rainy: Rain. Good day for the wheel. The clay likes the damp, and nobody comes to talk to me. Present company excepted.$u
tobin.dialogue.AcceptGift_330: Clay. You brought a potter clay.$u#$b#...It's good clay, too. Thank you.$h
tobin.dialogue.AcceptGift_709: Hardwood. That's a long, steady firing, that is. Thank you.$h
tobin.dialogue.AcceptGift_395: Coffee. Black. You've been paying attention.$h
tobin.dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Positi: For my birthday. ...Thank you. I'm not good at this part. It's a good gift.$l
tobin.dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Negati: For my birthday. Hm. I'll find it a shelf.$0
lupini.name: Lupini
lupini.gift.love: My friend! This is perfect. You've got an eye, you know. Don't waste it.$h
lupini.gift.like: How kind. The colour alone! Thank you.$h
lupini.gift.dislike: Ah. How... manufactured. Thank you, I suppose.$s
lupini.gift.hate: Oh, no. No, no. Take it away before I describe it.$a
lupini.dialogue.Introduction: Ah, my friend, you came all this way! Welcome to the Vale. You'll want the view from the overlook, then the tea, then the view again.$h#$b#I know you. Paint under the nails. A buyer like that is rare at the Night Market. Most of them want something to match the sofa.$u
lupini.dialogue.Mon: Look at that sky. Cobalt at the top, washed to bone at the edges. Overworked, if you ask me. Still, it has energy.$u
lupini.dialogue.Tue: I could paint a Lupini in my sleep. Some days I think I do.$u
lupini.dialogue.Wed: The light here is the reason I stayed. Thirty years, and it still does something new every morning. Showing off, really.$h
lupini.dialogue.Thu: Down in the meadow today, my friend. Ochre and violet everywhere. Fern's work. She'd say it's the meadow's.$h
lupini.dialogue.Fri: The lake at noon is a terrible subject. Flat, white, no shadow at all. I paint it every Friday out of spite.$u
lupini.dialogue.Sat: The painter in the forest? We nod. It's a very meaningful nod.$u
lupini.dialogue.Sun: Sunday. Even I don't paint on Sundays. I stand at the easel and think about painting, which is much less messy.$0
lupini.dialogue.Mon2: I owe that critic, Julian Vane, everything. I've never forgiven him for it.$u
lupini.dialogue.Wed2: Tobin and I have argued about whether a bowl is art for fifteen years. He thinks he's winning. Let him have that.$h
lupini.dialogue.Fri2: Emmett is the only one in the Vale who laughs at me. To my face, I mean. Everyone else does it behind the hedges.$u
lupini.dialogue.Mon4: They call me 'Famous Painter Lupini' at the market. As if it were my first name. My mother would be so pleased, and so confused.$u
lupini.dialogue.Tue4: One review, in a Zuzu City paper, when I was thirty. Suddenly everything I painted was a Lupini. I wasn't sure what that was. I'm still not.$s
lupini.dialogue.Wed4: Bea keeps my tab. She pretends to be strict about it. I pretend to be frightened. It's our arrangement.$h
lupini.dialogue.Thu4: You walked straight past the best thing in the meadow. That puddle by the path. The sky's in it, upside down and cleaner.$u
lupini.dialogue.Fri4: Fern has let the ivy grow right over my studio window. I've never asked her to cut it. The light comes through green. I've grown fond of green.$l
lupini.dialogue.Sat4: A buyer told me once she loved my work because it matched her curtains. I sold it to her. I think about that more than I should.$s
lupini.dialogue.Sun4: Do you paint every day? Don't. Paint when it's fun. ...Listen to me. Advice I've never once taken.$u
lupini.dialogue.Tue6: I stood at the easel all morning and didn't make a single stroke. It happens more than I let on.$s
lupini.dialogue.Thu6: The Old Studios were full when I came. Twenty of us, shouting about colour over breakfast. Now there's me, and I don't shout.$s
lupini.dialogue.Sat6: You ask good questions, my friend. You ask them and then you wait. Painters never wait. We fill the space with ourselves.$h
lupini.dialogue.Mon8: Do you know, I haven't painted anything for myself in twenty years. I didn't notice until you asked.$s
lupini.dialogue.Tue8: I painted something badly yesterday. On purpose. A cow. It was wonderful. It looked like a sofa with opinions.$h
lupini.dialogue.Wed8: If nobody ever saw what you made, would you still want to make it? I've started asking myself. I don't like how long the answer takes.$s
lupini.dialogue.Thu8: The meadow again today. No commission, no buyer. Just me and the violets, being honest with each other.$h
lupini.dialogue.Fri8: I've been watching how you look at things. You stop. Most people don't stop. Stay like that, my friend.$l
lupini.dialogue.Sat8: Sable and I should talk properly one day. We're the same story, told from opposite ends. I'm sure they know it too.$s
lupini.dialogue.Sun8: Come and sit with me at the overlook sometime, early, before anyone's awake. That's the best light there is.$h
lupini.dialogue.spring_Mon: Spring! Every green on the palette at once. Vulgar. Glorious.$h
lupini.dialogue.spring_Thu: Blossom on the old tree. It comes down like a bad watercolour, far too much white. I adore it.$h
lupini.dialogue.summer_Tue: Summer evenings, Emmett and I walk the Vale. He sings. I correct his colours. Neither of us improves.$u
lupini.dialogue.summer_Fri: The heat flattens everything by noon. Paint before ten or after five, my friend. In between, have lunch.$0
lupini.dialogue.fall_Wed: Fall. The Vale earns its name. Gold leaf everywhere, for free. I've never painted it right. Nobody has.$h
lupini.dialogue.fall_Sat: Open House soon. No judges, no prizes. Just people looking at things. Imagine!$h
lupini.dialogue.winter_Tue: Winter strips the Vale back to its drawing. I like seeing the bones, like a sketch before the paint goes on.$0
lupini.dialogue.winter_Sat: My boat's nearly packed for the Night Market. Nine paintings, three years, one a night. Everyone thinks it's a mystery. It's a schedule.$u
lupini.dialogue.spring_1: First of spring, my friend. Everything starts over. Even me, possibly.$h
lupini.dialogue.summer_1: Summer. The light gets loud. I look at it over my glasses and pretend it was my idea.$u
lupini.dialogue.fall_1: Fall. Gold, rust, ochre. The Vale is finally dressed as itself.$h
lupini.dialogue.winter_1: Winter. Grey on grey on white. Harder to paint than it looks. Most things are.$0
lupini.dialogue.nightmarket: The market tonight! I'll be on the boat, looking mysterious. It takes a great deal of effort, looking mysterious.$u
lupini.dialogue.winter_18: Home from the market, and it's my birthday. Every year I sell a painting the night before. A very good present, to myself.$h
lupini.dialogue.rainy: Rain. Wet light, my friend, the best kind. Everything goes dark and shining like a varnished panel. I won't paint it. I'll just stand here.$0
lupini.dialogue.AcceptGift_348: Wine! Look at the colour of it. Garnet, going brown at the rim. I'll drink it slowly.$h
lupini.dialogue.AcceptGift_402: Sweet pea from the Vale's banks. Fern will be cross it isn't still growing. I'll paint it before it fades.$h
lupini.dialogue.AcceptGift_395: Coffee! You've saved my morning, and possibly the painting.$h
lupini.dialogue.AcceptGift_330: Clay. Tobin's given me enough clay to last a lifetime, my friend. He calls it 'perspective'.$u
lupini.dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Posit: For my birthday! You remembered. I'm touched, my friend. Truly.$l
lupini.dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Negat: For my birthday. Ah. It has... a strong composition.$s
fern.name: Fern
fern.gift.love: Oh! Oh, you lovely thing. And you, too. Thank you!$h
fern.gift.like: Thank you! Something to plant, or something to plant near. Either way.$h
fern.gift.dislike: Oh. Thank you. I'll find somewhere for it. Somewhere well away from the beds.$s
fern.gift.hate: Not near the soil! Never near the soil.$a
fern.dialogue.Introduction: Mind the clover! Not you, the clover. Well. Both of you.$h#$b#I'm Fern. Fern Aster. Yes, two plants. My parents had one joke. I look after the gardens. Or they look after me. It changes.$u
fern.dialogue.Mon: Monday. I go to town for seeds and come home with more seeds than I went for. Every Monday.$h
fern.dialogue.Tue: A garden isn't finished. It's just having a good year.$0
fern.dialogue.Wed: Hello, you. No, not you, the foxgloves. ...Hello to you too.$u
fern.dialogue.Thu: The statues in the garden have a moss on them that grows nowhere else. Somebody from the city wants it scraped off. Over my dead body.$a
fern.dialogue.Fri: I took flowers up to Bea this morning. She'll say they wilted. They're wildflowers, Bea!$u
fern.dialogue.Sat: Do you plant in rows? Everybody plants in rows. It's all so... tidy.$0
fern.dialogue.Sun: Sundays are for walking the meadow and doing nothing. I pull weeds the whole time. I can't help it.$u
fern.dialogue.Mon2: Rows. So many rows. Don't you ever let anything just... happen?$u
fern.dialogue.Wed2: Tobin pretends to be put out when I bring him flowers for his glazes. He uses every single one.$h
fern.dialogue.Fri2: Emmett writes songs about my plants. Terrible songs. I hum them all day.$a
fern.dialogue.Mon4: My teacher was nearly ninety when I came. He talked to every plant in the Vale by name. I thought he was mad. Now I do it.$s
fern.dialogue.Tue4: Lupini's window is all ivy now. He's never asked me to cut it back. I think he likes the green light. I know I do.$h
fern.dialogue.Wed4: There's a vine in my seedhouse that only flowers at night. I've sat up for it three years running. Fell asleep every time.$u
fern.dialogue.Thu4: I keep a mushroom in a pot that I swear hums. Nobody else can hear it. That's fine. It's not humming for them.$u
fern.dialogue.Fri4: People want the gardens put back how they were. Hedges cut square, paths swept. That was a hundred years ago. The garden's moved on.$a
fern.dialogue.Sat4: You've got dirt under your nails too. Good. I don't trust clean hands. Except Bea's. She's frightening.$h
fern.dialogue.Sun4: The bees are back in the meadow. I counted them. Well, I tried. They don't hold still.$h
fern.dialogue.Tue6: Sometimes I think 'let it grow' is just a nice way of saying I can't keep up. Don't tell anyone I said that.$s
fern.dialogue.Thu6: Evelyn gave me a rose cutting last week. Caroline gave me tea leaves. I gave them both moss. They were very polite about it.$u
fern.dialogue.Sat6: You listen to the garden. I can tell. You go quiet when you walk through it.$l
fern.dialogue.Mon8: My teacher said a gardener's job is to listen. I think I've only been arguing.$s
fern.dialogue.Tue8: I've been thinking about clearing one path through the sculpture garden. Just one. To see the statues properly. Maybe.$0
fern.dialogue.Wed8: I'm saving you a cutting from the night vine. It isn't ready yet. Nothing worth having is ready yet.$l
fern.dialogue.Thu8: I meant to leave the Vale when my teacher died. Then I planted something, and had to stay to see it come up. Then another. That was eight years ago.$h
fern.dialogue.Fri8: Come and walk the meadow with me sometime. You don't have to say anything. The meadow does most of the talking.$h
fern.dialogue.Sat8: Your farm's lovely. Even the rows. I've decided to forgive the rows.$h
fern.dialogue.Sun8: I like it when you visit. The garden likes it too. Well, I'm guessing. It hasn't said.$l
fern.dialogue.spring_Tue: Spring! Everything's coming up at once, and every bit of it wants something. Water, sun, me.$h
fern.dialogue.spring_Fri: Crocuses in the sculpture garden, right where the old paths were. They remember the paths better than we do.$0
fern.dialogue.summer_Wed: Summer Spangle all over the meadow. It looks like someone spilled a jar of paint and walked off. I love that.$h
fern.dialogue.summer_Sat: It's so hot the snapdragons are sulking. I don't blame them.$u
fern.dialogue.fall_Mon: Fall's when I collect seed. Every plant in the Vale gives me a little packet of next year. Polite of them.$h
fern.dialogue.fall_Thu: The leaves are gold all over the statues. Some people would sweep them up. I'm not some people.$u
fern.dialogue.winter_Wed: Winter. Nothing grows, so I fuss over the seedhouse instead. The seedlings find me exhausting.$u
fern.dialogue.winter_Sat: I spent all afternoon brushing snow off the statues. They looked cold. I know they're stone.$s
fern.dialogue.spring_1: Spring! Did you hear that? That's everything waking up at once. Well, I heard it.$h
fern.dialogue.fall_1: Fall. Seed season. My pockets will be full of seed till winter, and I'll be finding it in the wash till spring.$u
fern.dialogue.winter_1: Winter. The garden's asleep. I'm meant to be resting too. I'm not very good at it.$0
fern.dialogue.summer_15: It's my birthday! I plant something every year for it. One day the meadow will be all my birthdays.$h
fern.dialogue.rainy: Rain! The whole Vale's having a drink. I'm potting in the seedhouse and listening to it. Best sound there is.$h
fern.dialogue.AcceptGift_347: A Rare Seed! I'm going to plant it somewhere nobody will expect, and wait. Thank you!$h
fern.dialogue.AcceptGift_Moss: Moss! The good kind, from somewhere old. I know exactly which statue wants this.$h
fern.dialogue.AcceptGift_402: Sweet pea! You picked it, didn't you. ...Well. It's still lovely. I'll press it.$h
fern.dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Positiv: For my birthday? You darling. You muddy darling. Thank you!$h
fern.dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Negativ: For my birthday. Oh. I'll keep it. Well away from the garden.$s
fern.dialogue.AcceptBouquet: A bouquet. They were alive this morning, you know.$s#$b#...But it's tradition. And it's from you. All right. Yes.$l
fern.dialogue.RejectBouquet_VeryLowHeart: Cut flowers, for me? We've only just met. And they've only just died.$a
fern.dialogue.RejectBouquet_LowHearts: That's sweet. But I don't know you well enough yet. Put them in water, at least.$s
fern.dialogue.RejectBouquet: Oh. I'm flattered, I am. But not like that. I'm sorry.$s
fern.dialogue.RejectMermaidPendant: It's beautiful. But I'm not ready for that. Not yet.$s
fern.dialogue.RejectMermaidPendant_NeedH: Your house is lovely. It's just... small. Where would the seed drawers go?$u
fern.dialogue.dating_FernAster: Hello, you. Yes, you this time.$l
emmett.name: Emmett
emmett.gift.love: Now that's a gift. Thank you, truly. I'll write a verse about it. Possibly two.$h
emmett.gift.like: Ha! Lovely, thank you. That's going straight in a song.$h
emmett.gift.dislike: Hm. Very shiny. What does it do?$0
emmett.gift.hate: Oh. That's... I'll hold it at arm's length, if that's all right.$a
emmett.dialogue.Introduction: A new face! I'll need a verse for you. What rhymes with 'farmer'? ...I'll work on it.$h#$b#Emmett. I play the fiddle, mostly at people who didn't ask. Welcome to the Vale.$u
emmett.dialogue.Mon: Monday morning, empty seats, the stage all mine. Best audience I've ever had. Never once threw anything.$u
emmett.dialogue.Tue: Half these songs, I'm the last person alive who knows them. That's a lot of pressure for a fiddle.$0
emmett.dialogue.Wed: I came for a week. Five years ago. The week's going well.$h
emmett.dialogue.Thu: Down by the water with my notebook. I'm writing a song about fish. It's not going well. Nothing rhymes with trout.$u
emmett.dialogue.Fri: Friday night by the fire at the Vale House. I play, Bea pretends not to sing, Tobin pretends not to tap his foot.$h
emmett.dialogue.Sat: Saturdays I walk the whole Vale, end to end, and hum whatever it sounds like. Today it sounds like a reel.$h
emmett.dialogue.Sun: Sunday. Slow tunes only. Bea's rule. She says fast ones curdle the milk.$u
emmett.dialogue.Mon2: Lupini paints like he's being watched. I play like nobody's listening. One of us has it right.$u
emmett.dialogue.Wed2: Tobin made me an ocarina. I play it badly, on purpose, outside his window. It's the least I can do.$h
emmett.dialogue.Fri2: I've written three songs about Fern's plants. She says she hates them. She's been heard humming the one about the turnips.$u
emmett.dialogue.Mon4: I've played in a hundred towns. I couldn't tell you which one I'm from.$s
emmett.dialogue.Tue4: Some of my favourite songs came from ordinary folk. A ferryman. A farmer's widow, way up north. They never wrote them down. So I keep them.$0
emmett.dialogue.Wed4: This amphitheatre sat empty for decades. You can feel it waiting, if you stand on the stage long enough. Or that's my knees.$u
emmett.dialogue.Thu4: My nan said amethyst is good for the throat. I keep one in my pocket. I still can't hit the high notes.$u
emmett.dialogue.Fri4: Bea and I squabble like an old married couple. We're not. She'd never have me. She's seen the state of my coat.$u
emmett.dialogue.Sat4: I've been on the road since I was eighteen. Festivals, weddings, wakes. I've played more wakes than I'd like. People want a tune when they've got no words.$s
emmett.dialogue.Sun4: There's a note this valley makes of an evening, when the wind comes down off the falls. I've been trying to find it on the fiddle for five years.$0
emmett.dialogue.Tue6: Every spring I pack my bag. Every spring I don't leave. I haven't told anyone that. Well. Now I have.$s
emmett.dialogue.Thu6: Sam wants to learn the fiddle. He doesn't know it yet, but he does. He's coming along nicely, for someone hiding behind the jukebox.$u
emmett.dialogue.Sat6: You're easy to play for. You actually listen. Most people hear the tune and miss the words.$l
emmett.dialogue.Mon8: I've been writing something. About the Vale, and the people in it. It's the first song I've ever written about somewhere I live.$l
emmett.dialogue.Tue8: You know what I've never had? A song about home. I've got one from every town in Ferngill, and none of my own.$s
emmett.dialogue.Wed8: Funny. I used to count the days till I'd move on. Lately I've lost count.$l
emmett.dialogue.Thu8: The river's got a better voice than me. I've stopped competing and started harmonising.$h
emmett.dialogue.Fri8: There's a verse in the new song I haven't played for anyone. Don't ask. ...You can ask a bit.$l
emmett.dialogue.Sat8: I walked the whole Vale this morning and didn't once think about the road out. That's new.$h
emmett.dialogue.Sun8: Stay a while, @. Sit. I'll play you something slow. Bea's rule.$h
emmett.dialogue.spring_Tue: Spring, and the swallows are back on the amphitheatre steps. Better rhythm than the last drummer I played with.$u
emmett.dialogue.spring_Fri: I walked in here five springs ago, sat on those stone seats and played to nobody. Nobody clapped. I stayed anyway.$0
emmett.dialogue.summer_Wed: Summer evenings, Lupini and I walk the Vale. He tells me what colour everything is. I tell him what key. Neither of us listens.$h
emmett.dialogue.summer_Sun: Too hot to play. Too hot to sing. I'm humming, which is the least effort music can be.$u
emmett.dialogue.fall_Tue: Open House is coming. I'll play the amphitheatre all afternoon. If it's cleared by then. If it isn't, I'll play to the brambles.$u
emmett.dialogue.fall_Thu: Chanterelles in the woods. Tastes like autumn, that. I could live on them. I very nearly have.$h
emmett.dialogue.winter_Mon: Winter. Cold fingers, stiff strings, slow tunes. The fiddle sulks till spring.$s
emmett.dialogue.winter_Fri: I've moved into the armchair by Bea's fire for the season. She's threatening rent. I'm paying in jigs.$u
emmett.dialogue.spring_1: First of spring. I always used to leave on the first of spring. Look at me, still here.$h
emmett.dialogue.summer_1: Summer! Festival season. Back on the road. Not that I'm on the road. Habit.$u
emmett.dialogue.fall_1: Fall. I've got a song for this. Twelve verses, all about leaves. I'll spare you.$u
emmett.dialogue.winter_1: Winter. The road's closed, as far as my feet are concerned. The fire's open.$h
emmett.dialogue.spring_9: It's my birthday. Same week I first walked into the Vale. Five years ago. Or thirty-five. Depends how you count.$h
emmett.dialogue.rainy: Rain. I stay in on days like this and write. Mostly I write the first line six times and make tea.$u
emmett.dialogue.AcceptGift_281: A chanterelle! Tastes like autumn, this. Thank you.$h
emmett.dialogue.AcceptGift_303: Pale Ale. You're a friend for life now, I'm afraid. No take-backs.$h
emmett.dialogue.AcceptGift_236: Pumpkin soup! I've had it in a hundred towns. This one's going to be the best. I can tell.$h
emmett.dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Posit: For my birthday? You remembered! I've never stayed anywhere long enough for anyone to remember.$l
emmett.dialogue.AcceptBirthdayGift_Negat: For my birthday. Hm. It's the thought. Thank you for the thought.$s
emmett.dialogue.AcceptBouquet: For me? Flowers?$l#$b#Well. I'm not going anywhere, then. Am I.$l
emmett.dialogue.RejectBouquet_VeryLowHea: That's a lot of flowers for a stranger. I'll write you a song instead. It'll be short.$u
emmett.dialogue.RejectBouquet_LowHearts: That's sweet. Let's get to know each other first. I've a habit of leaving.$s
emmett.dialogue.RejectBouquet: I'm flattered. Truly. But I'm not the one for you. I'm sorry.$s
emmett.dialogue.RejectMermaidPendant: That's... a lot. I'm not ready to promise anybody anything. Not yet.$s
emmett.dialogue.RejectMermaidPendant_Nee: Where would I put the fiddle? Where would I put me? Let's wait till there's room.$u
emmett.dialogue.dating_EmmettWren: Hello, you. I've written a verse about you. It's not finished. It might never be finished. That's a compliment.$l
bea.shop.tea: The tea's fresh. The biscuits are yesterday's, which is when biscuits are best.
bea.shop.cups: Mind the cups. They're Tobin's, and they'd survive a fall off the roof. The floor wouldn't.
bea.shop.soup: There's always soup. It's the one thing in this inn that's never broken.
bea.shop.closed: Nobody's at the counter. A card by the bell: 'Back in a minute. Probably. -B'
bea.counter: "What'll it be? Tea, food, a bed? We do all three, two of them well."
bea.counter.bell: There's a bell on the counter and a slate of today's food. Nobody seems to mind if you help yourself.
bea.counter.away: Nobody's at the counter. A card by the bell: 'Back in a minute. Probably. -B'
bea.room.booked: There. Upstairs, first door on the left. Breakfast is whenever you come down. The stairs creak, so I'll know.
bea.room.already: You're in the room upstairs, first door on the left. The bed's made, and the roof over it is one of the good two.
bea.room.money: It's two hundred for the night. Come back when the farm's been kind to you.
bea.room.locked: A card on the pillow: 'Booked. Ask Bea at the counter downstairs.'
bea.artists.locked: A card pinned to the door, in Bea's hand: 'The Artists' Room. Not let out. -B'
bea.room.tucked: You woke up in the guest bed. Bea must have found you on the floor and put you to bed.
bea.room.tucked.paid: You woke up in the guest bed. Bea found you on the floor and put you to bed. She took {0}g for the room.
fern.shop.rows: Plant them anywhere. Not in rows. I'll know.
fern.shop.moss: The moss is from the old statues. Don't tell the heritage society.
fern.shop.packets: I folded every packet myself. The lumpy ones are the good ones.
fern.shop.closed: Wildflower seeds in packets she folded herself, and a sign: 'Plant them anywhere. Not in rows. Back at five. -F'
tobin.shop.shelf: Everything on the shelf's for sale. Nothing's insured.
tobin.shop.clay: Good clay. Red, from the pit. Keep it damp or it sulks.
tobin.shop.pots: Pots for growing things in. Fern says I don't make enough of them. Fern says a lot.
tobin.shop.closed: A cash tin and a few bowls on the counter, and a smooth patch in the wood where his elbows rest. A note on the tin: 'Out. -T'
opal.shop.welcome: Come in, come in! Mind the glass. Anything that sparkles, ask me. Anything sharp, ask Jet.$h
opal.shop.city: That lamp's from the city. Awful thing. Buy it anyway, we need the shelf.
opal.shop.windows: A window changes a room more than anything you can put in it. I'd stake the studio on that. I very nearly did.$h
jet.shop.tags: Prices are on the tags. Opal wrote them. Ignore the little hearts.
jet.shop.cut: Cut it this morning. It'll outlast the house.
glass.shop.closed: Suncatchers turning on a brass rail, a little lamp, a cash tin. A card in two hands: 'Out!! Back soon!! -O', and under it, smaller: 'Back at two. -J'
lupini.letter.title: From Lupini
lupini.letter: My friend,^^The Night Market's packed away, and I'm home in the Gilded Vale. You have paint under your nails, so you should see it. Pam's bus has a second stop now. She grumbles about it, which means she's pleased.^^Come and see the light. I'll show you where to stand.^   -Lupini
town.pam.opened: Got myself a second stop on the route now. Some valley full of painters, out past the woods. Lewis says it's good for business. My back says otherwise.
town.pam.visited: Seen the Vale now, have you? Pretty place. Long drive, mind. Mind you don't leave your hoe on my seats.
town.lewis.opened: The bus to the Gilded Vale is running again! When I was a boy, half the painters in the Republic passed through there. I hear the inn's still standing. Just about.
town.lewis.visited: How was the Vale? Is the inn's roof still on? Mostly? Good, good. Mostly is better than most roofs.
town.gus.opened: Someone from the Gilded Vale left a note on my bar. 'Heard you do a good soup. Mine's better. -B.'$h#$b#I like her already.
town.gus.visited: Been out to the Vale? Did Bea feed you? She'll have fed you. Did she mention me? ...No reason.
town.sable.opened: Lupini wrote to you, then. He writes to everyone eventually.$u#$b#We nod. If you see him, tell him I said nothing. He'll understand.
town.sable.visited: You went to the Vale. Did you see the light come off the lake in the morning?#$b#...Don't tell him I asked.$u
town.elliott.opened: The Gilded Vale is open again. Its painters filled whole galleries, once. I've always longed to write there. Perhaps the light will forgive my prose.$h
town.elliott.visited: You've been to the Vale! Tell me everything. No, tell me one thing, slowly.$h
town.leah.opened: The Gilded Vale... I went there once, years ago. The sculpture garden.$s#$b#I never went back. Ask me another time.
town.evelyn.opened: There's a young lady at the Gilded Vale who grows the loveliest wildflowers, I'm told. I do hope she visits. I've a rose cutting with her name on it.$h
town.caroline.opened: If you go out to the Vale, the gardener there trades tea leaves for cuttings. Tell her Caroline sent you.$h
town.clint.opened: Heard the potter out at the Vale has a kiln that runs hotter than my forge.#$b#...I'd like to see that. Not that I'd tell him.
town.robin.opened: The Vale's got a potter, I hear. Real clay planters! Demetrius says we have enough planters. Demetrius is wrong.$h
town.sam.opened: There's a fiddle player out at the Vale who's played, like, every town in Ferngill. Every one! I'm gonna ask him for lessons.$h#$b#Or watch him from really far away.
town.haley.opened: They say the trees in the Gilded Vale go actual gold in the fall. Like, gold. I need to photograph that.$h
town.julian.opened: The Gilded Vale. I reviewed a painter from there once, when I was young and generous. I forget his name.$u#$b#It was a very good review. I'm told he's done well out of it.
town.margot.opened: The Gilded Vale's open again? There'll be paintings in those old studios nobody's looked at in thirty years. I'll need gloves. Lots of gloves.$h
bea.letter.title: Bea's hash browns
bea.letter: @,^^Somebody has to look after you, and it may as well be me. These are my breakfast hash browns. Guests come back for them, not for the roof.^^Don't tell Gus. He'll want them for the Saloon, and I'll have to say no, and he'll sulk.^^ -Bea
tobin.letter.title: Clay
tobin.letter: @,^^Ten of the good clay, from the pit. Keep it damp. Wedge it before you use it. Don't let Lupini near it, he'll want to paint it.^^ -T.
fern.letter.title: Seeds
fern.letter: Hello you,^^Here's a packet of my flower mix. Plant it somewhere you'll forget about, then don't weed it.^^I'll know if you plant it in a row.^^ -Fern
emmett.letter.title: For the throat
emmett.letter: @,^^My nan swore by these for the throat. I've never once hit the high notes, but she was usually right about things.^^I've started a verse about you. It's not finished. Most of mine aren't.^^ -Emmett
lupini.postcard.title: From the boat
lupini.postcard: My friend,^^The first night of the market. The lanterns on the water are the colour of ripe apricots, and nobody looks at them. They look at the paintings.^^Come and find me on the boat. I'll be looking mysterious. It's very tiring.^^ -L.
vale.hall.mural: The Vale, painted by the artists who lived here, one long summer. Each of them added one thing. The paint is flaking now.
vale.hall.jade_hills: 'Jade Hills.' Oil on canvas, painted from the overlook. The artist's name has worn off the frame.
vale.hall.eco_hill: 'A Night On Eco-Hill.' The first painting ever hung in this hall, says the old catalogue.
vale.hall.kitemaster: 'Kitemaster '95.' Left to the Vale by a painter who went to the city and never came back.
vale.hall.boat: 'Boat.' Painted on the lake at dawn. The rowboat is still out there.
vale.hall.needlepoint: 'Needlepoint Flower.' Stitched, not painted. The Vale's artists argued for a week about whether to hang it.
vale.hall.panel: Studies of the Vale by its past artists, pinned up here so they wouldn't be lost.
vale.hall.panel_b: A sunset over the lake, unsigned. Someone has pencilled 'too orange' on the back.
vale.hall.bowls: Bowls from Tobin's kiln. A note in his handwriting: 'They're for using. Don't just look at them.'
vale.hall.jug: A jug from Tobin's kiln, slip white and slate blue. 'Land of Clay' was painted at the pit its clay came from.
vale.hall.flowers: Wildflowers from the Vale's meadow, pressed and labelled by Fern. Some of the labels are jokes.
vale.hall.flowers_b: More of Fern's pressed flowers. One label just says 'Do not water.'
vale.hall.spiral: 'Spiral.' Carved from river stone found below the falls, and set on a block of the same slate.
vale.hall.heron: 'Heron.' Bronze, on the green marble plinth its sculptor brought from the coast. She refused to show it on anything else.
vale.hall.kiln_woman: 'Kiln Woman.' Terracotta, fired in the pottery's kiln long before Tobin's time. Her plinth is bricks from the kiln's first chimney.
vale.hall.moss_figure: 'Moss Figure.' Its sandstone plinth was the old studios' doorstep, and the moss came with it. Fern says that moss only grows on old statues.
vale.hall.visitors_book: The Hall's visitors' book. Its first pages are full of names from long ago.
vale.hall.poster: A poster for the Vale's last exhibition. The date has faded away.
vale.hall.vista: 'Vista.' Still hanging where it was left the night the last exhibition closed.
vale.hall.calico_falls: 'Calico Falls.' A painter's souvenir of the desert, says the old label.
vale.hall.sheeted: Paintings under a dust sheet. Nobody has lifted it in years.
vale.hall.crates: Packing crates. One was opened, and never closed again.
vale.hall.crates_b: Crates of frames, waiting to go back to artists who never came for them.
vale.hall.ladder: The ladder they used to hang the last exhibition.
vale.hall.unshown: A sculpture that never made it out to the gallery.
vale.hall.frame_rack: Empty frames, saved for paintings nobody has painted yet.
vale.hall.dancing_grass: 'Dancing Grass.' Too tall for the gallery's walls, so it hangs back here.
vale.hall.ledger: The Hall's ledger: every painting ever shown here, in the same careful handwriting.
vale.hall_closed.mural: The Vale, painted by the artists who lived here. Nobody could take it down when the Hall closed. Dust has settled along the top of it.
vale.hall_closed.panel: A display under a dust sheet. Something tall.
vale.hall_closed.panel_b: Another tall shape under a dust sheet. A corner of a gilt frame shows at the bottom.
vale.hall_closed.case: A glass case under a dust sheet. Something inside clinks when you touch it.
vale.hall_closed.case_b: A glass case under a dust sheet. Through a moth hole: something pressed flat, and a paper label.
vale.hall_closed.statue_round: Something round and heavy under a dust sheet, on its plinth. It feels like stone.
vale.hall_closed.statue_moss: A figure under a dust sheet. Moss has crept up the hem of it.
vale.hall_closed.statue_kiln: A figure under a dust sheet, on a plinth of old bricks.
vale.hall_closed.statue_heron: Something tall and thin under a dust sheet. It seems to be standing on one leg.
vale.hall_closed.desk: The front desk under a dust sheet. A corner of the visitors' book pokes out.
vale.hall_closed.bench: A bench under a dust sheet, still facing the mural.
vale.hall_closed.frames: The paintings from the walls, taken down and leaning under a sheet.
vale.hall_closed.hook: A nail, and a paler square where a painting hung.
vale.studio.unfinished: An unfinished painting of the Vale at sunset. Half of it is still pencil lines. Nobody knows who painted it.
vale.studio.note: A folded note in a careful hand. It isn't addressed to anyone.
vale.studio.sketches: Charcoal studies for the painting on the easel: the valley, a figure, a pair of hands, over and over.
vale.studio.backward: A painting turned to face the wall. Someone hung it that way, and never turned it back.
vale.studio.window: The tall north window, grey with dust. Painters chose this studio for its light.
vale.studio.trestle: A trestle crusted with years of paint, in every colour the Vale has.
vale.studio.cot: A bed with a thin, worn mattress. Whoever worked here slept here too.
vale.studio.washstand: A cracked jug in a dry basin.
vale.studio.trunk: A trunk, locked. The key is nowhere to be found.
vale.studio.rules: THE OLD STUDIOS. HOUSE RULES.^1. No turpentine after ten.^2. Return the ladder.^3. The north light is shared. One morning each.^4. Whoever took the good brushes: we know.^^Under the rules, a column of signatures, each in its own ink.
vale.studio2.racks: Sheets of coloured glass stood on end in their rack. When the sun's on them, Opal's half of the floor goes every colour at once.
vale.studio2.designs: Opal's designs for windows, coloured in and pinned up any old how. Three more are half under the bed.
vale.studio2.drafting: Opal's drawing board. A window half coloured in, and every pencil she owns, none of them sharpened.
vale.studio2.window: The studio's big window. Mabel Corrie worked under this light for twenty-four summers.
vale.studio2.mabel_window: Mabel's last design, finished by Jet at her own bench. The Vale at dawn, the river running gold between the trees.
vale.studio2.bench: Mabel's bench, worn pale where her arms rested. Her pliers are laid out as she left them. Nobody sits here.
vale.studio2.bench_used: Mabel's bench, in use again. Her pattern book lies open beside a panel half leaded.
vale.studio2.light_table: A light table glowing under a half-leaded panel. Every piece is cut to the line, exactly.
vale.studio2.kiln: A sleek steel kiln from the city, with a dial and a little red light. It cost more than the studio.
vale.studio2.cutting_bench: Jet's bench: a cutting mat, a sheet of clear glass scored once, and his tools laid out in a straight row.
vale.studio2.offcuts: Offcuts of glass sorted by colour, ruby, amber, cobalt and green. Not one piece is in the wrong tray.
vale.studio2.ladder: The ladder up to the loft. Whatever's up there has been there since the twins left.
vale.studio2.city_lamp: A lamp from their flat in Zuzu City. It's the most expensive thing in the Vale, and it looks it.
vale.studio2.glass_lamp: A lamp they made themselves, ruby, amber and cobalt. The city lamps have gone up to the loft.
vale.studios.sign: THE OLD STUDIOS^^I. The north light.^Agnes Morrow, oils. 18 summers.^Teodor Lisle, oils. 11 summers.^Celia Marsh, portraits. 7 summers.^(The last name has weathered away.)^^II.^Hollis Pike, woodcuts. 22 summers.^Mabel Corrie, stained glass. 24 summers.^The Corrie twins, stained glass. 8 summers.^^III.^Bram Fairlie, carving. 31 summers.^Ida Venn, watercolours. 12 summers.
vale.studios.plaque_1: Studio I, carved over the door. Most of its gold has flaked away. There was a name painted under it once.
vale.studios.plaque_2: Studio II, carved over the door. Under it, in faded paint: The Corrie twins, glass.
vale.studios.plaque_3: Studio III, carved over the door. Under it, in faded paint: Ida Venn, watercolours.
vale.pottery.kiln: The kiln: the reason Tobin came to the Vale. On firing days you can feel it from the door.
vale.pottery.hardwood: Hardwood for the kiln, stacked just so. Tobin knows if a single log has moved.
vale.pottery.wheel: Tobin's wheel. The kick plate is worn into a dip the exact shape of his clog.
vale.pottery.wheel_b: A second wheel, for whoever he's teaching. There's a lot more clay on the floor around this one.
vale.pottery.drying_rack: Pots drying before their firing. Tobin says the hard part is leaving them alone.
vale.pottery.glazes: Jars of glaze, labelled in pencil: ash, iron, crushed quartz. One just says 'Fern's idea.'
vale.pottery.pot_shelf: Plates, jugs and bowls in terracotta and slate. A card says: 'Everything here is for sale. Nothing is insured.'
vale.pottery.pot_shelf_b: His slip-white ware, plain as milk. Ask Tobin what a bowl means and he'll tell you it holds soup.
vale.pottery.price_board: Prices in chalk, rubbed out and rewritten. Planters have gone up. Nobody has complained yet.
vale.pottery.counter: The counter, a cash tin and a few bowls on it. There's a smooth patch in the wood where his elbows rest.
vale.pottery.crate: An order packed in straw, for the Vale House. Bea's cups, again.
vale.pottery.clay: Clay from his pit by the river. He digs it himself, on Sundays.
vale.pottery.tools: His tools on pegs: ribs, wires, loop tools. One peg is empty. That rib lives in his apron pocket.
vale.pottery.bookcase: Books on glazes, kilns and clay, and one novel, read so often its spine has split in two.
vale.pottery.bed: Tobin's bed, made with square corners. He's up at dawn to check on the kiln.
vale.atelier.painting_1: 'Clouds.' He painted it lying on his back in the meadow. It took all summer, because the clouds wouldn't sit still.
vale.atelier.painting_2: 'Solar Kingdom.' Painted in one long afternoon, he says. He's been trying to paint that afternoon again ever since.
vale.atelier.painting_3: 'Portrait Of A Mermaid.' Ask Lupini who sat for it, and he only smiles.
vale.atelier.painting_4: 'Land Of Clay.' Painted at Tobin's clay pit. Tobin says the colours are wrong, and has looked at it longer than anyone.
vale.atelier.painting_5: 'Three Trees.' They grow up by the overlook. He swears there used to be four.
vale.atelier.painting_6: 'The Serpent.' It hangs where the morning sun doesn't reach. He says it prefers that.
vale.atelier.painting_7: 'Tropical Fish,' number 173. He won't say what became of the other hundred and seventy-two.
vale.atelier.display_easel: 'Red Eagle,' set where the light from the door falls on it. Visitors always look at it first, which is the point.
vale.atelier.empty_hook: An empty nail, and a paler square of wallpaper. Its painting went to the Night Market on his boat, to someone with a sofa to match.
vale.atelier.easel: His easel, and a canvas he started in the spring. The paint on the palette has dried to a skin.
vale.atelier.window: The big north window: painters want north light, the same all day. Ivy has crept over one corner, and he's never asked Fern to cut it back.
vale.atelier.hat_stand: His wide straw hat, and an indigo smock gone stiff with ochre at the cuffs.
vale.atelier.bust: A plaster bust for drawing practice. Someone has given it a moustache in charcoal.
vale.atelier.bench: A bench to sit and look. Lupini says most people give a painting three seconds. He'd like to see you try thirty.
vale.atelier.paint_table: A palette, tubes squeezed from the middle, jars of brushes. He has a favourite brush and won't say which.
vale.fern.vine: A vine on a trellis, its buds shut tight. Fern says it only flowers at night, and only when it feels like it.
vale.fern.mushroom: A mushroom in a pot. Fern swears it hums. If you hold very still... no. Probably not.
vale.fern.seed_drawers: Dozens of little drawers, each labelled in her hand. 'Sweet Pea.' 'Crocus.' 'Do not open (bees).'
vale.fern.potting_bench: Her potting bench against the glass: pots, soil, a trowel worn thin. She talks to the seedlings while she works.
vale.fern.seed_counter: Wildflower seeds in packets she folded herself. A sign: 'Plant them anywhere. Not in rows.'
vale.fern.seed_trays: Seedlings in trays, each with a little name stick. Some of the names are just encouragement.
vale.fern.pressed_flowers: Wildflowers from the meadow, pressed and framed. She only picks them once they've gone to seed, so nothing misses out.
vale.fern.pressed_flowers_b: More pressed flowers. The oldest frame holds a sprig from her old teacher's garden.
vale.fern.soil: Compost from her own heap. She's proud of it, and given half a chance she'll tell you why.
vale.fern.watering_can: A dented watering can, never quite empty.
vale.fern.bed: Fern's bed, with a leaf on the pillow. There's always a leaf somewhere.
vale.emmett.maps: Maps of everywhere Emmett has played, pinned up, with string running from town to town. There's no pin in the Vale.
vale.emmett.instruments: His fiddle, a concertina with one broken key, and the clay ocarina Tobin made him. He plays the ocarina badly, on purpose.
vale.emmett.music_stand: A song in progress. Half of it is crossed out; the other half has 'better?' written over it.
vale.emmett.coat: His long travel-worn coat and the faded red neckerchief. He won't hear of a new coat.
vale.emmett.desk: Scraps of paper, a pencil chewed to a stub, a notebook stuffed with verses. He writes here when it rains.
vale.emmett.trunk: The trunk he travelled with, still half packed. He says it's easier that way.
vale.emmett.songbooks: Songbooks from every town in Ferngill, some in his own handwriting. For half these songs, he's the last one who knows them.
vale.emmett.stump: A mossy stump for a guest to sit on. Emmett says chairs make people stay too long.
vale.emmett.crate: A crate for a side table. 'FRAGILE' on the side: it carried the concertina here. It didn't help the key.
vale.emmett.bed: A bed under the eaves, a patchwork quilt from a market up north. He meant to stay a week.
vale.house.guestbook: The inn's guest book. This year's pages are mostly blank. Bea calls the clientele 'select.'
vale.house.china: Bea's good china, too good to use. Everything else in the tea room is Tobin's.
vale.house.teapots: Teapots in every size. Bea knows which one each regular likes, and never has to ask.
vale.house.counter: The counter: a cake under glass, the till, and Lupini's tab, which needs a drawer of its own.
vale.house.tea_table: A tea table, set with Tobin's cups. Bea says they're too heavy, and won't use any others.
vale.house.piano: The inn's old piano. Emmett says it's in tune with itself, if not with anything else.
vale.house.clock: The hall clock runs ten minutes fast. That's how Bea's great-aunt liked it, and Bea's never had the heart to fix it.
vale.house.photo: A photograph of the Vale House long ago, every window full of faces. A small girl on the step is scowling at the camera.
vale.house.fireplace: The snug's fire. Emmett plays here in the evenings, if somebody buys him a slice of pie first.
vale.house.bear: A big blue bear, for visitors' children. Bea won't admit she gave it a name.
vale.house.dollhouse: A dollhouse of the Vale House, every room in it. Two of them have roofs.
vale.house.kitchen: The kitchen: the only room that matters, says Bea. The plumbing has other ideas.
vale.house.lighthouse: A lighthouse on a rocky coast, painted by a guest who missed the sea. The Vale is a long way from it.
vale.house.guest_easel: An easel in the guest room, for guests who paint. In the Vale, that's most of them.
vale.house.guest_desk: A writing desk, a candle, and the inn's notepaper. 'Wish you were here' is already printed at the top.
vale.house.canvases: Canvases left by artists who stayed here. Bea's great-aunt took paintings when they couldn't pay the rent.
vale.house.lighthouse_easel: A lighthouse, half painted. Whoever started it left in a hurry, or ran out of blue.
vale.house.blank_canvases: Blank canvases leaning on the bed's foot, waiting for whoever stays next.
vale.house.accounts: The inn's accounts, in Bea's tidy hand. The column for repairs is a good deal longer than the column for guests.
vale.house.flowers: A painting of flowers that never wilt. Bea hung it to make a point to Fern.
fish.loach.name: Claybank Loach
fish.loach.description: A little red fish that lives in the clay banks of the river, the same colour as the mud it hides in.
fish.trout.name: Cascade Trout
fish.trout.description: Leaps up the cascades when the rain swells the river. Nothing rhymes with it.
fish.sculpin.name: Falls Sculpin
fish.sculpin.description: Hides under the river stones below the falls, and comes out on cold nights.
fish.shiner.name: Lakeblue Shiner
fish.shiner.description: So blue that the painters who saw it were told they'd made it up.
fish.carp.name: Gilt Carp
fish.carp.description: Rises in the fall, when the Gilded Tree's leaves drift down onto the lake.
vale.studios.sale.plaque_2_forsale: A notice is pinned over the old gold II: FOR SALE. Enquire at the Vale House.
vale.studios.sale.plaque_2_sold: SOLD, pasted across the notice. Somebody's bought Studio II.
vale.studios.sale.plaque_2_works: SOLD. Chalked on the scaffold pole: ROBIN'S CARPENTRY. MIND THE PLANKS.
vale.studios.sale.plaque_2_renovated: Studio II, the numeral new in gold. Under it, freshly painted: Opal & Jet Corrie, glass.
vale.studios.sale.plaque_3_forsale: A notice is pinned over the old gold III: FOR SALE. Enquire at the Vale House.
vale.studios.sale.plaque_3_sold: SOLD, pasted across the notice. Somebody's bought Studio III.
vale.studios.sale.plaque_3_works: SOLD. Chalked on the scaffold pole: ROBIN'S CARPENTRY. MIND THE PLANKS.
vale.studios.sale.plaque_3_new: The plaque's been sanded down to bare wood. The old gold numeral's gone. A card tucked in the door frame says: T. Brand.
vale.studios.sale.plaque_3_carved: Studio III, cut into the bare wood by hand. No gold. Under it, a card in the door frame: T. Brand, woodcarver.
vale.studios.sale.timber: Sawn planks, stacked on bearers to keep them off the wet. Stencilled on the end of every one: ROBIN.
vale.studios.sale.letter: Hi! A heads-up from the shop.^^I've taken a job out in the Gilded Vale: one of the Old Studios has sold, and somebody wants it fit to live in by the end of the month. So on weekdays until then I'll be out there with my toolbox.^^The shop's still open. If I'm not behind the counter, leave your order and the money in the box and I'll see to it. And if you've got building work on the farm, that comes first, the Vale can wait a day.^^   -Robin
vale.studios.sale.letter.title: Robin's away on a job
vale.studios.sale.robin_away: Robin's not here. A note on the counter: 'Out in the Gilded Vale on a job, back this evening. Orders in the box, I'll see to them. -R'
vale.studios.sale.robin_book: Her order book lies open beside the box.
